chapter_seo_title: The Golden Throne: Li Huowang's Memory-Eating Palace Trap
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang enters the golden Throne Hall of the Great Liang Palace, only to discover time and memory are being erased. Beneath the golden bricks, a Heart-Turbid corpse waits, sewn shut with swastikas.
og_title: The Golden Throne: Memory Erasure and a Buried Heart-Turbid
og_description: Li Huowang's search for the Zuowandao leads him into a golden palace that eats memories. He finds his own desperate carvings on his arm—and a buried Heart-Turbid corpse serving as a formation eye.
twitter_title: Li Huowang vs. the Golden Memory-Eating Palace
twitter_description: The Great Liang Palace isn't just gold—it's a trap. A Heart-Turbid corpse sewn with swastikas lies beneath the Throne Hall.

lore_anchors.definition: In traditional Chinese symbolism, a five-clawed dragon represents the emperor. A sixth claw here signals a corrupted or escalated form of imperial power.
The Jinluan Dian was the most important ceremonial hall in a Chinese palace. Here, it is literalized into a solid gold trap.
A sacred Buddhist symbol of auspiciousness, here corrupted into a binding, sealing curse that entangles the Heart-Turbid corpse.
The complete set of hexagrams from the I Ching, representing all states of change in the universe. Their appearance in the sky suggests a cosmic principle or observer.
The central node of a ritual or supernatural formation; destroying or removing it usually collapses the entire array.
